notes: Replaced solver, dependable-computation and grammar-of-trust language with instruction, calculation and checkable interpretation. Preserved the language’s proposal status and cross-language design source.
Every spoken sentence independently checked against the canonical English source for clear purpose, intended viewer response, source fidelity and natural spoken wording.
All scenes remain compact, with one sentence per clip and specific restrained delivery directions. Viewer responses are editorial intentions, not results from audience testing.

sentenceIntentions.text: The computer gets the calculation right, but it has misunderstood the instruction.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Expose an exact result built on mistaken meaning.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Immediately understand why calculation and interpretation are different problems.

sentenceIntentions.text: Executable Natural Language proposes clearer ways to express instructions so people can check what software will do.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Introduce the source-specific proposal before the example develops.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand the new idea and want to see how the book tests it.
sentenceIntentions.ttsDirection: Explain the proposed idea in a warm, ordinary voice; emphasize the concrete choice the listener can inspect, without announcing a proven breakthrough.

sentenceIntentions.text: Small words such as same, we, and must can leave important choices unstated.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make ambiguity visible in ordinary vocabulary.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Notice that common words carry unstated decisions.

sentenceIntentions.text: People often fill those gaps without noticing; a computer needs an interpretation it can act on.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Explain why software makes those choices consequential.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand what humans silently supply during conversation.

sentenceIntentions.text: Its proposed language, SLEnglish, aims to make those hidden choices visible.

sentenceIntentions.text: Comparisons with other languages show how familiar grammar can hide distinctions that matter.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Give a distinctive reason to read this book.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Become curious about lessons other languages offer to software design.

sentenceIntentions.text: If you work with AI or code, those small decisions may matter more than you expect.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect the topic to a reader’s practical interests.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to look before the calculation, where meaning is chosen.

sentenceIntentions.text: Before asking whether the answer is correct, how do we check that the machine understood the question?
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Close on the central unresolved check.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Ask how fidelity to the original question can be established.
